claim: Zap70 catalytic activity is required for CTL-mediated killing of P815 target cells.
source: When we examined the ability of Zap70(AS) CTL to induce target cell death in the presence of the 3-MB-PP1 inhibitor, we saw a complete abrogation of killing (Figure 1A).
evidence: Experimental data from cytotoxicity assays showing loss of killing with inhibitor treatment, presented in Figure 1A.

claim: Zap70 catalytic activity is required for IFN-γ, TNF-α and IL-2 cytokine production by CTL.
source: CTL with an inactive Zap70 demonstrated a loss of IFN-γ, TNF-α and IL-2 cytokine production (Figure 1B).
evidence: FACS analysis data showing loss of cytokine production with Zap70 inhibition, presented in Figure 1B.

claim: Zap70(AS) CTL form conjugates with P815 target cells at 60% frequency in the presence of 3-MB-PP1.
source: Zap70-inactive CTL were able to bind and form conjugates with target cells almost as well as Zap70-active CTL, with 60% of Zap70(AS) CTL (n = 70) forming conjugates in the presence of 3-MB-PP1 compared with 67% (n = 60) without inhibitor.
evidence: Quantitative microscopy data showing conjugate formation percentages.

claim: Zap70(AS) CTL form conjugates with P815 target cells at 67% frequency in the absence of 3-MB-PP1.
source: Zap70-inactive CTL were able to bind and form conjugates with target cells almost as well as Zap70-active CTL, with 60% of Zap70(AS) CTL (n = 70) forming conjugates in the presence of 3-MB-PP1 compared with 67% (n = 60) without inhibitor.
evidence: Quantitative microscopy data showing conjugate formation percentages.

claim: Zap70 catalytic activity is required for talin clearance into a ring at the pSMAC.
source: When activated Zap70(AS) CTL were conjugated to P815 target cells in the presence of 3-MB-PP1, their ability to clear talin into a ring at the pSMAC was impaired (Figure 2A).
evidence: Confocal microscopy data showing impaired talin ring formation with Zap70 inhibition, presented in Figure 2A.

claim: Talin accumulates across the synapse when Zap70 is catalytically inhibited.
source: Instead, accumulation of talin labelling was seen across the synapse, when viewed in the z plane (Figure 2A, inset).
evidence: Confocal microscopy data showing talin distribution in z-plane reconstructions, presented in Figure 2A inset.

claim: Zap70 catalytic activity is required for Lck accumulation at the cSMAC.
source: cSMAC formation was also impaired, because the same conjugates displayed a drastic reduction in the accumulation of Lck and PKC-θ at the cSMAC (Figure 2B,C).
evidence: Confocal microscopy data showing reduced Lck clustering with Zap70 inhibition, presented in Figure 2B.

claim: Zap70 catalytic activity is required for PKC-θ accumulation at the cSMAC.
source: cSMAC formation was also impaired, because the same conjugates displayed a drastic reduction in the accumulation of Lck and PKC-θ at the cSMAC (Figure 2B,C).
evidence: Confocal microscopy data showing reduced PKC-θ clustering with Zap70 inhibition, presented in Figure 2C.

claim: Talin is required for F-actin polarisation to the synapse.
source: Previous data have demonstrated that talin is required for F-actin polarisation to the synapse (Wernimont et al., 2011).
evidence: Supported by citation to Wernimont et al., 2011.

claim: 76.5% of conjugates formed with Zap70-active CTL show actin clearance into a ring at the dSMAC.
source: The majority of conjugates formed with Zap70-active CTL accumulate actin at the contact site, which clears into a ring of actin at the dSMAC of the synapse (76.5%, n = 65) (Figure 3B, black) consistent with other studies of CTL (Tsun et al., 2011; Zhao et al., 2012).
evidence: Quantitative confocal microscopy data showing actin clearance percentages, presented in Figure 3B.

claim: 26% of conjugates formed with Zap70-inactive CTL show actin clearance.
source: In contrast, when CTL lack Zap70 catalytic activity, they lose this ability, and the proportion of conjugates displaying clearance drops to 26% (n = 83) (Figure 3B).
evidence: Quantitative confocal microscopy data showing reduced actin clearance with Zap70 inhibition, presented in Figure 3B.

claim: 91.5% of conjugates lacking a cSMAC fail to clear actin when Zap70 is catalytically inhibited.
source: When actin clearance is examined in conjugates which do not display a cSMAC (75%, n = 83), the effect is even more pronounced, with 91.5% of conjugates failing to clear actin.
evidence: Quantitative confocal microscopy data analyzing actin clearance in conjugates without cSMAC.

claim: Actin accumulates at the synapse in the absence of Zap70 catalytic activity.
source: Interestingly, accumulation of actin at the synapse was still observed in the absence of Zap70 activity (Figure 3C).
evidence: Confocal microscopy data showing actin accumulation despite Zap70 inhibition, presented in Figure 3C.

claim: Phosphorylated ERK co-localises with actin at the immune synapse.
source: Previous studies have shown that phosphorylated ERK may play a role in actin reorganisation as ERK co-localises with actin at the immune synapse, is implicated in granule and MTOC polarisation, and is required for CTL degranulation (Robertson et al., 2005; Jenkins et al., 2009).
evidence: Supported by citations to Robertson et al., 2005 and Jenkins et al., 2009.

claim: ERK is implicated in granule and MTOC polarisation.
source: Previous studies have shown that phosphorylated ERK may play a role in actin reorganisation as ERK co-localises with actin at the immune synapse, is implicated in granule and MTOC polarisation, and is required for CTL degranulation (Robertson et al., 2005; Jenkins et al., 2009).
evidence: Supported by citations to Robertson et al., 2005 and Jenkins et al., 2009.

claim: ERK is required for CTL degranulation.
source: Previous studies have shown that phosphorylated ERK may play a role in actin reorganisation as ERK co-localises with actin at the immune synapse, is implicated in granule and MTOC polarisation, and is required for CTL degranulation (Robertson et al., 2005; Jenkins et al., 2009).
evidence: Supported by citations to Robertson et al., 2005 and Jenkins et al., 2009.

claim: Zap70 phosphorylation on tyrosine 319 does not depend on Zap70 catalytic activity.
source: Inhibition of Zap70 catalytic activity does not impair its capacity to be phosphorylated on tyrosine 319, which is inducibly phosphorylated upon CD3 crosslinking, and remains similarly phosphorylated in the presence of a high concentration of 3-MB-PP1 (10 μM).
evidence: Western blot analysis showing Zap70 Y319 phosphorylation with and without inhibitor treatment.

claim: Zap70 is a substrate of the upstream Src kinase Lck.
source: This result is consistent with Zap70 as a substrate of the upstream Src kinase Lck.
evidence: Inference from the observation that Zap70 Y319 phosphorylation persists when Zap70 catalytic activity is inhibited, combined with established knowledge.

claim: LAT phosphorylation depends on Zap70 catalytic activity.
source: However, the phosphorylation of LAT, a substrate of Zap70, as well as PLCγ and ERK all depend on Zap70 catalytic activity.
evidence: Western blot analysis showing loss of LAT phosphorylation with Zap70 inhibition, presented in Figure 4A.

claim: PLCγ phosphorylation depends on Zap70 catalytic activity.
source: However, the phosphorylation of LAT, a substrate of Zap70, as well as PLCγ and ERK all depend on Zap70 catalytic activity.
evidence: Western blot analysis showing loss of PLCγ phosphorylation with Zap70 inhibition, presented in Figure 4A.

claim: ERK phosphorylation depends on Zap70 catalytic activity.
source: However, the phosphorylation of LAT, a substrate of Zap70, as well as PLCγ and ERK all depend on Zap70 catalytic activity.
evidence: Western blot analysis showing loss of ERK phosphorylation with Zap70 inhibition, presented in Figure 4A.

claim: A signalling pathway from Zap70 via the LAT signalosome and PLCγ is required for activation of ERK in CTL.
source: These results suggest a signalling pathway from Zap70 via the LAT signalosome and PLCγ is required for activation of ERK in CTL.
evidence: Inference from western blot data showing Zap70-dependent phosphorylation of LAT, PLCγ, and ERK.

claim: A PI3K-dependent pathway is required for activating ERK and CTL degranulation.
source: It has also been reported that a PI3K-dependent pathway is required for activating ERK and CTL degranulation (Robertson et al., 2005).
evidence: Supported by citation to Robertson et al., 2005.

claim: Akt phosphorylation is sensitive to Zap70 inhibition.
source: Indeed, Akt phosphorylation was sensitive to Zap70 inhibition, suggesting that ERK is activated downstream of Zap70 through a LAT and PLCγ pathway or alternatively through a pathway that also includes AKT.
evidence: Western blot analysis showing loss of Akt phosphorylation with Zap70 inhibition, presented in Figure 4A.

claim: ERK is activated downstream of Zap70 through a LAT and PLCγ pathway or alternatively through a pathway that also includes AKT.
source: Indeed, Akt phosphorylation was sensitive to Zap70 inhibition, suggesting that ERK is activated downstream of Zap70 through a LAT and PLCγ pathway or alternatively through a pathway that also includes AKT.
evidence: Inference from western blot data showing Zap70-dependent phosphorylation of LAT, PLCγ, ERK, and Akt.

claim: Integrin activation occurs in the absence of Zap70 catalytic activity in naïve CD4 T cells.
source: Since our previous studies had shown that integrin activation occurs in the absence of Zap70 catalytic activity in naïve CD4 T cells (Au-Yeung et al., 2010), we asked whether the integrin-mediated activation of Vav-1 (Gao et al., 2005) was seen in CTL in which Zap70 catalytic activity was inhibited.
evidence: Supported by citation to Au-Yeung et al., 2010.

claim: Vav-1 plays an important role in both TCR- and integrin-mediated activation of actin reorganisation in T cells.
source: This was of particular interest because Vav-1 has been shown to play an important role in both TCR- and integrin-mediated activation of actin reorganisation in T cells (del Pozo et al., 2003, Garcia-Bernal et al., 2009; Tybulewicz, 2005).
evidence: Supported by citations to del Pozo et al., 2003, Garcia-Bernal et al., 2009, and Tybulewicz, 2005.

claim: TCR activation triggers Vav-1 phosphorylation independently of Zap70 kinase activity.
source: We found that TCR activation triggers Vav-1 phosphorylation independently of Zap70 kinase activity, with Vav-1 phosphorylation occurring in both Zap70+/− and Zap70(AS) CTL lysates from cells treated with 3-MB-PP1, both for overall Vav-1 phosphorylation as well as at Y160, a site that is selectively phosphorylated upon TCR stimulation or αvβ3 integrin-mediated activation (Gao et al., 2005; Miletic et al., 2006).
evidence: Western blot analysis of Vav-1 phosphorylation with and without Zap70 inhibition, presented in Figure 4B, combined with citations to Gao et al., 2005 and Miletic et al., 2006.

claim: Vav-1 Y160 is selectively phosphorylated upon TCR stimulation or αvβ3 integrin-mediated activation.
source: We found that TCR activation triggers Vav-1 phosphorylation independently of Zap70 kinase activity, with Vav-1 phosphorylation occurring in both Zap70+/− and Zap70(AS) CTL lysates from cells treated with 3-MB-PP1, both for overall Vav-1 phosphorylation as well as at Y160, a site that is selectively phosphorylated upon TCR stimulation or αvβ3 integrin-mediated activation (Gao et al., 2005; Miletic et al., 2006).
evidence: Supported by citations to Gao et al., 2005 and Miletic et al., 2006.

claim: Zap70 catalytic function makes only a minimal contribution to Vav-1 phosphorylation.
source: Only a slight decrease in Vav1 phosphorylation is evident in Zap70(AS) CTL with 10 μM 3MB-PP1 suggesting Zap70 catalytic function makes only a minimal contribution to Vav-1 phosphorylation (Figure 4B).
evidence: Western blot analysis showing minimal reduction in Vav-1 phosphorylation with Zap70 inhibition, presented in Figure 4B.

claim: Vav-1 phosphorylation and GEF activation occur independently of Zap70 catalytic activity.
source: These results suggest that Vav-1 phosphorylation, and presumably its GEF activation, occurs independently of Zap70 catalytic activity, while the pathway leading to ERK and PI3K activation are dependent on Zap70 catalytic activity.
evidence: Inference from western blot data showing Vav-1 phosphorylation persists with Zap70 inhibition.

claim: The pathway leading to ERK activation is dependent on Zap70 catalytic activity.
source: These results suggest that Vav-1 phosphorylation, and presumably its GEF activation, occurs independently of Zap70 catalytic activity, while the pathway leading to ERK and PI3K activation are dependent on Zap70 catalytic activity.
evidence: Western blot data showing loss of ERK phosphorylation with Zap70 inhibition.

claim: The pathway leading to PI3K activation is dependent on Zap70 catalytic activity.
source: These results suggest that Vav-1 phosphorylation, and presumably its GEF activation, occurs independently of Zap70 catalytic activity, while the pathway leading to ERK and PI3K activation are dependent on Zap70 catalytic activity.
evidence: Western blot data showing loss of Akt phosphorylation (downstream of PI3K) with Zap70 inhibition.

claim: Integrin activation occurs in CTL in which Zap70 is catalytically inhibited.
source: This supports the idea that integrin activation occurs in CTL in which Zap70 is catalytically inhibited, as previously observed in Treg (Au-Yeung et al., 2010).
evidence: Inference from Vav-1 phosphorylation data combined with citation to Au-Yeung et al., 2010.

claim: TCR activation increases the percentage of Zap70+/− CTL binding to ICAM-1 from 20% to 30%.
source: TCR activation increased the percentage of CTL binding to ICAM-1 from 20% to 30% for Zap70+/− and from 16% to 34% for Zap70 (AS) CTL.
evidence: Adhesion assay data showing increased binding to ICAM-1 after TCR activation, presented in Figure 4—figure supplement 1.

claim: TCR activation increases the percentage of Zap70(AS) CTL binding to ICAM-1 from 16% to 34%.
source: TCR activation increased the percentage of CTL binding to ICAM-1 from 20% to 30% for Zap70+/− and from 16% to 34% for Zap70 (AS) CTL.
evidence: Adhesion assay data showing increased binding to ICAM-1 after TCR activation, presented in Figure 4—figure supplement 1.

claim: 3-MB-PP1 treatment results in 32% binding to ICAM-1 for Zap70+/− CTL.
source: 3-MB-PP1 treatment resulted in 32% binding for Zap70+/− and 25% for Zap70 (AS) CTL (Figure 4—figure supplement 1).
evidence: Adhesion assay data showing binding to ICAM-1 with inhibitor treatment, presented in Figure 4—figure supplement 1.

claim: 3-MB-PP1 treatment results in 25% binding to ICAM-1 for Zap70(AS) CTL.
source: 3-MB-PP1 treatment resulted in 32% binding for Zap70+/− and 25% for Zap70 (AS) CTL (Figure 4—figure supplement 1).
evidence: Adhesion assay data showing binding to ICAM-1 with inhibitor treatment, presented in Figure 4—figure supplement 1.

claim: There is residual Zap70 catalytic-independent integrin function.
source: While there does appear to be some reduction in CTL adhesion upon 3-MB-PP1 treatment, these data also suggest there is residual Zap70 catalytic-independent integrin function.
evidence: Inference from adhesion assay data showing partial but not complete loss of adhesion with Zap70 inhibition.

claim: CTL move with an average speed of 9 μm/min on an ICAM-1 surface when Zap70 is catalytically active.
source: We found no difference in the speed of movement on an ICAM-1 surface with CTL moving with an average speed of 9 μm/min when Zap70 was catalytically active or inactive (Videos 1 and 2; n>84 each).
evidence: Live cell imaging data measuring CTL movement speed, presented in Videos 1 and 2.

claim: CTL move with an average speed of 9 μm/min on an ICAM-1 surface when Zap70 is catalytically inactive.
source: We found no difference in the speed of movement on an ICAM-1 surface with CTL moving with an average speed of 9 μm/min when Zap70 was catalytically active or inactive (Videos 1 and 2; n>84 each).
evidence: Live cell imaging data measuring CTL movement speed, presented in Videos 1 and 2.

claim: Zap70 catalytic activity is not required for integrin activation in CTL.
source: These results support the idea that Zap70 catalytic activity is not required for integrin activation in CTL.
evidence: Inference from movement speed data showing no difference with Zap70 inhibition.

claim: Conjugate formation is not impaired in Zap70-inactive CTL.
source: Our finding that conjugate formation is not impaired in Zap70-inactive CTL also supports this model.
evidence: Inference from conjugate formation data showing similar percentages with and without Zap70 inhibition.

claim: Catalytically inhibited Zap70 can still participate in signal transduction without active catalysis by interacting with other signalling proteins via its phosphorylated tyrosines.
source: Importantly, catalytically inhibited Zap70 can still participate in signal transduction without active catalysis, by interacting with other signalling proteins via its phosphorylated tyrosines.
evidence: Inference from western blot data showing Zap70 phosphorylation persists with inhibitor treatment and established knowledge of protein-protein interactions.

claim: Zap70 forms a complex with the adapter protein Crk, which activates the GTPase Rap1, which subsequently regulates integrin-mediated adhesion.
source: These results in activated CTL are consistent with previous studies in naïve CD4 T cells, which demonstrated a Zap70 kinase-independent scaffold function, where Zap70 forms a complex with the adapter protein Crk, which activates the GTPase Rap1, which subsequently regulates integrin-mediated adhesion (Au-Yeung et al., 2010).
evidence: Supported by citation to Au-Yeung et al., 2010.

claim: Centrosome polarisation to the synapse is an important step in CTL killing.
source: Centrosome polarisation to the synapse is an important step in CTL killing, because centrosome docking at the plasma membrane is responsible for directing the cytolytic granules to the secretory cleft at the cSMAC.
evidence: Established knowledge about CTL killing mechanisms.

claim: Centrosome docking at the plasma membrane is responsible for directing the cytolytic granules to the secretory cleft at the cSMAC.
source: Centrosome polarisation to the synapse is an important step in CTL killing, because centrosome docking at the plasma membrane is responsible for directing the cytolytic granules to the secretory cleft at the cSMAC.
evidence: Established knowledge about CTL killing mechanisms.

claim: NK cells can polarise both centrosome and granules to the synapse in response to integrin activation alone.
source: Given that NK cells can polarise both centrosome and granules to the synapse in response to integrin activation alone (Bryceson et al., 2005), it was of interest to ask whether the centrosome could polarise in CTL in which Zap70 was catalytically inhibited but integrin activation could still occur.
evidence: Supported by citation to Bryceson et al., 2005.

claim: Lck is essential for docking of the centrosome at the plasma membrane in CTL.
source: Our previous studies have shown that Lck is essential for docking of the centrosome at the plasma membrane since when Lck expression is inducibly turned off in mature CTL, the centrosome polarises towards the immune synapse, but does not dock at the plasma membrane.
evidence: Reference to previous studies by the authors.

claim: When Lck expression is turned off in mature CTL, the centrosome polarises towards the immune synapse but does not dock at the plasma membrane.
source: Our previous studies have shown that Lck is essential for docking of the centrosome at the plasma membrane since when Lck expression is inducibly turned off in mature CTL, the centrosome polarises towards the immune synapse, but does not dock at the plasma membrane.
evidence: Reference to previous studies by the authors.

claim: In the absence of centrosome docking at the plasma membrane, the granules cannot be delivered to the immunological synapse and CTL killing is abolished.
source: In the absence of centrosome docking at the plasma membrane, the granules cannot be delivered to the immunological synapse and CTL killing is abolished (Tsun et al., 2011).
evidence: Supported by citation to Tsun et al., 2011.

claim: Zap70 is a substrate of Lck.
source: Zap70 is a substrate of Lck and its phosphorylation by Lck activates Zap70's kinase activity.
evidence: Established knowledge about TCR signaling pathway.

claim: Phosphorylation of Zap70 by Lck activates Zap70's kinase activity.
source: Zap70 is a substrate of Lck and its phosphorylation by Lck activates Zap70's kinase activity.
evidence: Established knowledge about TCR signaling pathway.

claim: 65% of conjugates with catalytically active Zap70 display centrosomes tightly polarised to the cSMAC.
source: The majority of conjugates (65%) with catalytically active Zap70, displayed centrosomes tightly polarised to the cSMAC (Figure 5B) (n = 118), in accordance with previously published work (Jenkins et al., 2009).
evidence: Quantitative confocal microscopy data showing centrosome polarization percentages, presented in Figure 5B, with citation to Jenkins et al., 2009.

claim: 54% of conjugates with catalytically inhibited Zap70 show a centrosome location >5 μm from the synapse.
source: In contrast, Zap70 inhibition disrupted centrosome polarisation, with 54% of 3-MB-PP1 treated conjugates showing a centrosome location >5 μm from the synapse (Figure 5B) (n = 85).
evidence: Quantitative confocal microscopy data showing impaired centrosome polarization with Zap70 inhibition, presented in Figure 5B.

claim: 44% of control Zap70(AS)+DMSO conjugates show granules tightly clustered to the synapse.
source: Although the majority (44%) of control (Zap70(AS)+DMSO) conjugates (n = 117) show granules tightly clustered to the synapse, conjugates treated with 3-MB-PP1 showed a loss of granule polarisation to the synapse (Figure 5D) (n = 92).
evidence: Quantitative confocal microscopy data showing granule polarization percentages, presented in Figure 5D.

claim: Conjugates treated with 3-MB-PP1 show a loss of granule polarisation to the synapse.
source: Although the majority (44%) of control (Zap70(AS)+DMSO) conjugates (n = 117) show granules tightly clustered to the synapse, conjugates treated with 3-MB-PP1 showed a loss of granule polarisation to the synapse (Figure 5D) (n = 92).
evidence: Quantitative confocal microscopy data showing loss of granule polarization with Zap70 inhibition, presented in Figure 5D.

claim: The loss of centrosome and granule polarisation in cells lacking Zap70 catalytic activity is consistent with the loss of cytotoxicity.
source: The loss of centrosome and granule polarisation in cells lacking Zap70 catalytic activity is consistent with the loss of cytotoxicity.
evidence: Inference connecting polarization defects to cytotoxicity defects.

claim: In contrast to NK cells, integrin activation is not sufficient for centrosome and granule polarisation to the synapse in CTL.
source: These results suggest that, in contrast to NK cells, integrin activation is not sufficient for centrosome and granule polarisation to the synapse.
evidence: Inference from data showing loss of polarization despite integrin activation in Zap70-inhibited CTL.

claim: Zap70-active OT-I CTL show the centrosome polarising to the contact site within 6 min of initial interaction with the target.
source: Live cell imaging of Zap70-active OT-I CTL show the centrosome polarising right up to the contact site within 6 min of initial interaction with the target (Figure 6; Video 3; n = 34).
evidence: Live cell imaging data showing centrosome polarization kinetics, presented in Figure 6 and Video 3.

claim: The centrosome begins to polarise towards the synapse in Zap70(AS) OT-I CTL treated with 3-MB-PP1 but fails to reach the contact site.
source: However although the centrosome begins to polarise towards the synapse in Zap70(AS) OT-I CTL treated with 3-MB-PP1, the centrosome fails to reach the contact site with the closest point of contact ∼3 μm at 6 min after initial contact (Figure 6; Video 4; n = 50).
evidence: Live cell imaging data showing aborted centrosome polarization with Zap70 inhibition, presented in Figure 6 and Video 4.

claim: In Zap-deficient CTL, centrosome polarisation begins but aborts before the centrosome docks at the contact site.
source: In each video examined from Zap-deficient CTL, centrosome polarisation began, but aborted before the centrosome docked at the contact site formed by the synapse.
evidence: Live cell imaging data showing consistent pattern of aborted centrosome polarization.

claim: Contact sites formed between CTL with active Zap70 and target cells at 25 and 40 minutes show typical secretory synapses with flat stretches of tight membrane interactions and a central secretory cleft.
source: At 25 (Figure 7A) and 40 (Figure 7C) minutes, the contact sites formed between CTL with active Zap70 and target cells show typical secretory synapses (Stinchcombe et al., 2001b) with flat stretches of tight membrane interactions between the cells surrounding a central intercellular gap between the two cell membranes, termed the secretory cleft.
evidence: Electron microscopy data showing synapse ultrastructure, presented in Figure 7A and 7C, with citation to Stinchcombe et al., 2001b.

claim: The secretory cleft forms an extracellular space containing heterogeneous membranous and granular material.
source: The cleft forms an extracellular space containing heterogeneous membranous and granular material.
evidence: Electron microscopy observations of secretory cleft contents.

claim: Centrioles, lytic granules and Golgi elements are polarised up to the CTL plasma membrane in the middle of the contact site, opposite the secretory cleft.
source: Centrioles, lytic granules and Golgi elements are polarised up to the CTL plasma membrane in the middle of the contact site, opposite the secretory cleft.
evidence: Electron microscopy observations of organelle positioning.

claim: At 40 min of CTL-target interaction, the target cell endoplasmic reticulum is slightly swollen and vacuolated, characteristic of target cell death.
source: At these stages of interaction, the target cell appears relatively intact although the endoplasmic reticulum at 40 min is slightly swollen and vacuolated, characteristic of target cell death (Figure 7C).
evidence: Electron microscopy observations of target cell morphology, presented in Figure 7C.

claim: By 60 min of CTL-target interaction, there is marked evidence of target cell death with extensive endoplasmic reticular vacuolation and swollen mitochondria.
source: By 60 min, there is marked evidence of target cell death with extensive endoplasmic reticular vacuolation and swollen mitochondria, with the CTL appearing to retract from an etiolated, dying target (Figure 7E).
evidence: Electron microscopy observations of target cell death, presented in Figure 7E.

claim: In the absence of Zap70 kinase activity, there is no evidence of tight, flat membrane–membrane associations between CTL and target.
source: In the absence of Zap70 kinase activity the ultrastructure of the synapse is very different (Figure 7B,D,F). There is no evidence of the tight, flat membrane–membrane associations between CTL and target.
evidence: Electron microscopy observations of synapse ultrastructure with Zap70 inhibition, presented in Figure 7B, D, F.

claim: Secretory clefts are absent in synapses formed by CTL lacking Zap70 kinase activity.
source: Secretory clefts are absent, and neither centrioles, Golgi cisternae nor lytic granules are polarised towards the target cells.
evidence: Electron microscopy observations of synapse ultrastructure with Zap70 inhibition.

claim: Centrioles, Golgi cisternae and lytic granules are not polarised towards target cells in CTL lacking Zap70 kinase activity.
source: Secretory clefts are absent, and neither centrioles, Golgi cisternae nor lytic granules are polarised towards the target cells.
evidence: Electron microscopy observations of organelle positioning with Zap70 inhibition.

claim: The contact site between CTL lacking Zap70 activity and targets is highly interdigitated, formed of long projections from the CTL surface.
source: Instead, the contact site is highly interdigitated, formed of long projections from the CTL surface (black arrowheads).
evidence: Electron microscopy observations of synapse morphology with Zap70 inhibition.

claim: The only points of contact between CTL lacking Zap70 activity and target are at the tips of projections.
source: Notably points of contact between CTL and target are restricted to the tips of projections, providing limited sites for receptor interactions between the cells.
evidence: Electron microscopy observations of contact points with Zap70 inhibition.

claim: Conjugates formed between CTL lacking Zap70 activity and targets after 25, 40 and 60 min of interaction show similar phenotypes.
source: Conjugates formed between CTL lacking Zap70 activity and targets after 25, 40 and 60 min of interaction show similar phenotypes.
evidence: Electron microscopy observations across multiple time points.

claim: There is no evidence of target cell death at 25, 40, or 60 min in conjugates formed by CTL lacking Zap70 activity.
source: There is no evidence of target cell death at any of these time points in these samples.
evidence: Electron microscopy observations of target cell morphology with Zap70 inhibition.

claim: The secretory cleft is absent in >85% of conjugates formed by Zap70(AS) CTL + 3-MB-PP1 at any time point.
source: Quantitation of the EM data reveal that with Zap70(AS) CTL + 3-MB-PP1 the secretory cleft is absent in >85% of conjugates analysed at any time point (Figure 7—figure supplement 1A)
evidence: Quantitative electron microscopy data, presented in Figure 7—figure supplement 1A.

claim: The centrosome is found at distances greater than 1 μm from the synapse in >70% of conjugates formed by Zap70(AS) CTL + 3-MB-PP1.
source: the centrosome is not docked and instead is found at distances greater than 1 μm from the synapse in >70% of conjugates (Figure 7—figure supplement 1B)
evidence: Quantitative electron microscopy data, presented in Figure 7—figure supplement 1B.

claim: Projections are present between CTL and target in conjugates formed by Zap70(AS) CTL + 3-MB-PP1.
source: and projections are present between CTL and target (Figure 7—figure supplement 1C).
evidence: Quantitative electron microscopy data, presented in Figure 7—figure supplement 1C.

claim: Zap70(AS) CTL without inhibitor show secretory clefts in >50% of conjugates observed at 25 and 40 min.
source: In contrast, in the absence of inhibitor Zap70(AS) CTL showed secretory clefts in >50% of conjugates observed at 25 and 40 min, reduced to 27% only at 60 min, when many of the target cells were dead.
evidence: Quantitative electron microscopy data.

claim: Zap70(AS) CTL without inhibitor show secretory clefts in 27% of conjugates at 60 min.
source: In contrast, in the absence of inhibitor Zap70(AS) CTL showed secretory clefts in >50% of conjugates observed at 25 and 40 min, reduced to 27% only at 60 min, when many of the target cells were dead.
evidence: Quantitative electron microscopy data.

claim: 69% of conjugates formed by Zap70(AS) CTL without inhibitor at 25 min have at least one centriole <500 nm from the plasma membrane.
source: Tightly polarised centrosomes are seen most frequently at the 25 min time-point when 69% of conjugates have at least one centriole <500 nm from the plasma membrane and 85% of conjugates show no projections between CTL and target.
evidence: Quantitative electron microscopy data.

claim: 85% of conjugates formed by Zap70(AS) CTL without inhibitor at 25 min show no projections between CTL and target.
source: Tightly polarised centrosomes are seen most frequently at the 25 min time-point when 69% of conjugates have at least one centriole <500 nm from the plasma membrane and 85% of conjugates show no projections between CTL and target.
evidence: Quantitative electron microscopy data.

claim: Up to 60% of CTL lacking Zap70 catalytic activity show the centrosome within 3 μm of the synapse in conjugates formed at 25 min.
source: Interestingly up to 60% of CTL lacking Zap70 catalytic activity show the centrosome within 3 μm of the synapse in conjugates formed at 25 min (Figure 7—figure supplement 1B), consistent with the initial polarisation up to this point observed in live imaging (Figure 6), decreasing to 35% in conjugates formed at 60 min.
evidence: Quantitative electron microscopy data, presented in Figure 7—figure supplement 1B.

claim: 35% of CTL lacking Zap70 catalytic activity show the centrosome within 3 μm of the synapse in conjugates formed at 60 min.
source: Interestingly up to 60% of CTL lacking Zap70 catalytic activity show the centrosome within 3 μm of the synapse in conjugates formed at 25 min (Figure 7—figure supplement 1B), consistent with the initial polarisation up to this point observed in live imaging (Figure 6), decreasing to 35% in conjugates formed at 60 min.
evidence: Quantitative electron microscopy data, presented in Figure 7—figure supplement 1B.

claim: The ultrastructural morphology of the synapse formed by CTL lacking Zap70 activity resembles that seen in wild-type CTL at very early stages of synapse formation.
source: The unusual ultrastructural morphology of the synapse formed by CTL lacking Zap70 activity most closely resembles that seen in wild-type CTL at very early stages of synapse formation, when the target cell is intact and before the centrosome has polarised to the synapse (Figure 7G).
evidence: Comparison of electron microscopy images, presented in Figure 7G.

claim: At early stages of synapse formation in wild-type CTL, there are many interdigitations between CTL and target.
source: At this stage of synapse formation there are many interdigitations between CTL and target and neither the flattening of the membranes between the two cells, nor the secretory cleft are seen.
evidence: Electron microscopy observations of early synapse formation.

claim: At early stages of synapse formation in wild-type CTL, the contact points between CTL and target are only found at the tips of projections.
source: Here too the contact points between CTL and target are only found at the tips of projections between CTL and target.
evidence: Electron microscopy observations of early synapse formation.

claim: Loss of Zap70 catalytic activity arrests the reorganisation of membranes at the synapse at an early stage prior to formation of the secretory cleft.
source: These observations support the idea that loss of Zap70 catalytic activity arrests the reorganisation of membranes at the synapse at an early stage prior to formation of the secretory cleft.
evidence: Inference from electron microscopy data comparing Zap70-inhibited synapses to early wild-type synapses.

claim: The ultrastructure underlying the accumulation of actin across synapses formed by Zap70 catalytically inhibited CTL reveals actin-rich interdigitations.
source: Importantly these images reveal the ultrastructure that underlies the accumulation of actin seen across the synapses formed by Zap70 catalytically inhibited CTL and at the early stages of synapse formation in wild-type CTL, revealing the first link between the clearance of actin and the flattening of the membranes to form an extended area of contact during synapse formation.
evidence: Inference connecting electron microscopy observations to confocal microscopy observations of actin.

claim: There is a link between the clearance of actin and the flattening of the membranes to form an extended area of contact during synapse formation.
source: Importantly these images reveal the ultrastructure that underlies the accumulation of actin seen across the synapses formed by Zap70 catalytically inhibited CTL and at the early stages of synapse formation in wild-type CTL, revealing the first link between the clearance of actin and the flattening of the membranes to form an extended area of contact during synapse formation.
evidence: Inference from combined electron and confocal microscopy data.

claim: In the absence of Zap70 catalytic activity, formation of the immunological synapse is arrested at a stage where actin-rich interdigitations dominate the interface between the two cells.
source: We find that in the absence of Zap70 catalytic activity formation of the immunological synapse is arrested at a stage where actin-rich interdigitations dominate the interface between the two cells, with actin accumulated across the synapse and TCR unable to coalesce to form a cSMAC.
evidence: Summary of findings from confocal and electron microscopy data.

claim: In the absence of Zap70 catalytic activity, actin accumulates across the synapse.
source: We find that in the absence of Zap70 catalytic activity formation of the immunological synapse is arrested at a stage where actin-rich interdigitations dominate the interface between the two cells, with actin accumulated across the synapse and TCR unable to coalesce to form a cSMAC.
evidence: Confocal microscopy data showing actin distribution.

claim: In the absence of Zap70 catalytic activity, TCR is unable to coalesce to form a cSMAC.
source: We find that in the absence of Zap70 catalytic activity formation of the immunological synapse is arrested at a stage where actin-rich interdigitations dominate the interface between the two cells, with actin accumulated across the synapse and TCR unable to coalesce to form a cSMAC.
evidence: Confocal microscopy data showing loss of Lck clustering (marker of cSMAC).

claim: In the absence of Zap70 catalytic activity, the membranes between CTL and target are unable to flatten to provide an extended area of contact.
source: The membranes between CTL and target are unable to flatten to provide an extended area of contact and the secretory cleft does not form.
evidence: Electron microscopy data showing membrane morphology.

claim: In the absence of Zap70 catalytic activity, the secretory cleft does not form.
source: The membranes between CTL and target are unable to flatten to provide an extended area of contact and the secretory cleft does not form.
evidence: Electron microscopy data showing absence of secretory cleft.

claim: In the absence of Zap70 catalytic activity, signalling downstream of Zap70 is disrupted.
source: Signalling downstream of Zap70 is disrupted and neither centrosome nor granules polarise.
evidence: Western blot data showing loss of downstream signaling.

claim: In the absence of Zap70 catalytic activity, neither centrosome nor granules polarise.
source: Signalling downstream of Zap70 is disrupted and neither centrosome nor granules polarise.
evidence: Confocal and electron microscopy data showing loss of polarization.

claim: The Zap70(AS) mouse offers a unique opportunity to examine the role of the catalytic activity of Zap70 in CTL.
source: The Zap70(AS) mouse offers a unique opportunity to examine the role of the catalytic activity of Zap70 in CTL, which can be inhibited rapidly and specifically by addition of the inhibitor 3-MB-PP1.
evidence: Description of the experimental model and its advantages.

claim: Zap70 catalytic activity can be inhibited rapidly and specifically by addition of the inhibitor 3-MB-PP1 in the Zap70(AS) model.
source: The Zap70(AS) mouse offers a unique opportunity to examine the role of the catalytic activity of Zap70 in CTL, which can be inhibited rapidly and specifically by addition of the inhibitor 3-MB-PP1.
evidence: Description of the experimental model based on previous studies.

claim: Addition of 3-MB-PP1 to Zap70(AS) CD4 cells inhibits phosphorylation of LAT and ERK.
source: Previous studies using Zap70(AS) CD4 cells demonstrated that although addition of 3-MB-PP1 inhibits phosphorylation of LAT and ERK, Zap70 itself can still be phosphorylated and take part in signalling.
evidence: Reference to previous studies with Zap70(AS) CD4 cells.

claim: In Zap70(AS) CD4 cells treated with 3-MB-PP1, Zap70 itself can still be phosphorylated and take part in signalling.
source: Previous studies using Zap70(AS) CD4 cells demonstrated that although addition of 3-MB-PP1 inhibits phosphorylation of LAT and ERK, Zap70 itself can still be phosphorylated and take part in signalling.
evidence: Reference to previous studies with Zap70(AS) CD4 cells.

claim: The LAT signalosome and PLCγ are required for ERK activation in CTL.
source: Furthermore we show that phosphorylation of PLCγ, ERK and AKT are all dependent on Zap70 catalytic activity, suggesting that the LAT signalosome and PLCγ are required for ERK activation in CTL, providing a rationale for previous observations implicating both ERK (Robertson et al., 2005) and PLCγ (Le Floc'h et al., 2011) in CTL-mediated killing.
evidence: Inference from western blot data combined with citations to Robertson et al., 2005 and Le Floc'h et al., 2011.

claim: ERK is implicated in CTL-mediated killing.
source: Furthermore we show that phosphorylation of PLCγ, ERK and AKT are all dependent on Zap70 catalytic activity, suggesting that the LAT signalosome and PLCγ are required for ERK activation in CTL, providing a rationale for previous observations implicating both ERK (Robertson et al., 2005) and PLCγ (Le Floc'h et al., 2011) in CTL-mediated killing.
evidence: Supported by citation to Robertson et al., 2005.

claim: PLCγ is implicated in CTL-mediated killing.
source: Furthermore we show that phosphorylation of PLCγ, ERK and AKT are all dependent on Zap70 catalytic activity, suggesting that the LAT signalosome and PLCγ are required for ERK activation in CTL, providing a rationale for previous observations implicating both ERK (Robertson et al., 2005) and PLCγ (Le Floc'h et al., 2011) in CTL-mediated killing.
evidence: Supported by citation to Le Floc'h et al., 2011.

claim: Catalytically inactive Zap70 can be phosphorylated in CTL.
source: We also find that catalytically inactive Zap70 can itself be phosphorylated in CTL, supporting a kinase-independent scaffolding role for Zap70 in TCR regulation of integrin-mediated adhesion as reported in Treg cells (Au-Yeung et al., 2010).
evidence: Western blot data showing Zap70 phosphorylation with inhibitor treatment, combined with citation to Au-Yeung et al., 2010.

claim: Zap70 has a kinase-independent scaffolding role in TCR regulation of integrin-mediated adhesion.
source: We also find that catalytically inactive Zap70 can itself be phosphorylated in CTL, supporting a kinase-independent scaffolding role for Zap70 in TCR regulation of integrin-mediated adhesion as reported in Treg cells (Au-Yeung et al., 2010).
evidence: Inference from data combined with citation to Au-Yeung et al., 2010.

claim: The initial stages of synapse formation, during which there is an accumulation of actin across the synapse, may be integrin mediated.
source: These results support the idea that the initial stages of synapse formation, during which there is an accumulation of actin across the synapse, may well be integrin mediated.
evidence: Inference from data showing actin accumulation persists with Zap70 inhibition while integrin activation is maintained.

claim: Vav-1 phosphorylation mediated by the TCR, and possibly involving integrins, appears to be independent of Zap70 catalytic activity.
source: Consistent with this is our finding that Vav-1 phosphorylation mediated by the TCR, and possibly involving integrins (Riteau et al., 2003; Garcia-Bernal et al., 2005, 2009), appears to be independent of Zap70 catalytic activity, with Y160 phosphorylation occurring in Zap70 catalytically inactive CTL.
evidence: Western blot data showing Vav-1 phosphorylation with Zap70 inhibition, combined with citations to Riteau et al., 2003 and Garcia-Bernal et al., 2005, 2009.

claim: Zap70 has been implicated in the activation of Vav-1 both in vivo and in vitro.
source: Although earlier studies have implicated Zap70 in the activation of Vav-1 both in vivo (Deckert et al., 1996; Kadlecek et al., 1998; Michel et al., 1998) and in vitro (Brunati et al., 1995; Han et al., 1998), our present study shows phosphorylation of Vav-1 in the absence of Zap-70 catalytic activity, likely mediated by Lck.
evidence: Supported by citations to Deckert et al., 1996; Kadlecek et al., 1998; Michel et al., 1998; Brunati et al., 1995; and Han et al., 1998.

claim: Vav-1 phosphorylation in the absence of Zap-70 catalytic activity is likely mediated by Lck.
source: Although earlier studies have implicated Zap70 in the activation of Vav-1 both in vivo (Deckert et al., 1996; Kadlecek et al., 1998; Michel et al., 1998) and in vitro (Brunati et al., 1995; Han et al., 1998), our present study shows phosphorylation of Vav-1 in the absence of Zap-70 catalytic activity, likely mediated by Lck.
evidence: Inference from western blot data showing Vav-1 phosphorylation persists with Zap70 inhibition.

claim: Integrin-mediated actin dynamics proceed normally in Zap-inactive CTL.
source: Integrin-mediated actin dynamics proceed normally in Zap-inactive CTL. Not only is Vav-1 phosphorylated, but actin accumulates at the synapse and our live cell studies show that actin reorganisation required for integrin-mediated motility is unimpaired in the absence of Zap70 activity.
evidence: Multiple lines of data including Vav-1 phosphorylation, actin accumulation, and movement speed measurements.

claim: Actin reorganisation required for integrin-mediated motility is unimpaired in the absence of Zap70 activity.
source: Integrin-mediated actin dynamics proceed normally in Zap-inactive CTL. Not only is Vav-1 phosphorylated, but actin accumulates at the synapse and our live cell studies show that actin reorganisation required for integrin-mediated motility is unimpaired in the absence of Zap70 activity.
evidence: Live cell imaging data showing normal movement speed with Zap70 inhibition.

claim: The loss of Zap70 catalytic activity does not affect the integrin driven accumulation of actin at the synapse.
source: The loss of Zap70 catalytic activity does not affect the integrin driven accumulation of actin at the synapse, but results in loss of actin reorganisation once the synapse has formed.
evidence: Confocal microscopy data showing actin accumulation persists with Zap70 inhibition.

claim: Loss of Zap70 catalytic activity results in loss of actin reorganisation once the synapse has formed.
source: The loss of Zap70 catalytic activity does not affect the integrin driven accumulation of actin at the synapse, but results in loss of actin reorganisation once the synapse has formed.
evidence: Confocal microscopy data showing loss of actin clearance with Zap70 inhibition.

claim: When Zap70 is catalytically active, actin clears centrally, the membranes flatten into an extended area of contact and TCR microclusters coalesce to form the cSMAC.
source: When Zap70 is catalytically active actin clears centrally, the membranes flatten into an extended area of contact and TCR microclusters coalesce to form the cSMAC.
evidence: Summary of findings from confocal and electron microscopy data.

claim: Actin clearance is required for the coalescence of microclusters to form the cSMAC.
source: Our data are consistent with studies showing that actin clearance is required for the coalescence of microclusters to form the cSMAC (Campi et al., 2005; Babich et al., 2012; Beemiller et al., 2012; Yi et al., 2012) and we propose that this marks a transition from a highly interdigitated to a flattened interface between the two cells.
evidence: Supported by citations to Campi et al., 2005; Babich et al., 2012; Beemiller et al., 2012; and Yi et al., 2012.

claim: Actin clearance marks a transition from a highly interdigitated to a flattened interface between CTL and target cells.
source: Our data are consistent with studies showing that actin clearance is required for the coalescence of microclusters to form the cSMAC (Campi et al., 2005; Babich et al., 2012; Beemiller et al., 2012; Yi et al., 2012) and we propose that this marks a transition from a highly interdigitated to a flattened interface between the two cells.
evidence: Inference from combined electron and confocal microscopy data.

claim: Inhibition of Zap70 catalytic activity arrests the progress of synapse formation at an early stage.
source: In this study we find that inhibition of Zap70 catalytic activity arrests the progress of synapse formation at an early stage.
evidence: Summary of findings from multiple imaging modalities.

claim: Unlike NK cells, CTL are unable to polarise their centrosome and granules in response to integrin activation alone.
source: We find that, unlike NK cells (Bryceson et al., 2005), CTL are unable to polarise their centrosome and granules in response to integrin activation alone.
evidence: Data showing loss of polarization despite integrin activation, combined with citation to Bryceson et al., 2005.

claim: Zap70 has a role in controlling the reorganisation of membranes to form the interface at the immunological synapse, including the cSMAC and secretory cleft.
source: Our findings also reveal a surprising new role for Zap70 in controlling the reorganisation of membranes to form the interface at the immunological synapse, including the cSMAC and secretory cleft.
evidence: Summary of findings from electron and confocal microscopy data.

claim: Without membrane rearrangements at the synapse, the synapse is not functional.
source: Without these rearrangements, the synapse is not functional.
evidence: Inference from data showing loss of killing when membrane rearrangements are impaired.

claim: Zap70 has distinct roles as a structural protein regulating integrin-mediated control of actin vs the role of its catalytic subunit controlling TCR mediated control of actin and membrane remodelling during formation of the immunological synapse.
source: Our findings point to distinct roles played by Zap70 as a structural protein regulating integrin-mediated control of actin vs the role of it's catalytic subunit controlling TCR mediated control of actin and membrane remodelling during formation of the immunological synapse.
evidence: Summary and interpretation of all findings from the study.
